gaps.lead: She'll be on a flight, so she can't join the call.
gaps.sentence: She'll be on a flight, so ___ join the call.
gaps.explanation: won't be able to = future inability.

gaps.lead: No changes will be made to this project.
gaps.hint: go ahead = proceed; according to plan
gaps.explanation: 'No changes' means the project 'will go ahead according to plan'.

gaps.lead: I don't expect the company to make a profit this year, given the economic climate.
gaps.sentence: Given the economic climate, ___ the company made a profit this year.
gaps.hint: don't expect = would be surprised if + past
gaps.explanation: A tentative prediction: 'I would be surprised if + past simple'.

gaps.lead: Do you mind if I come over to see you later?
gaps.sentence: Do you ___ coming over to see you later?
gaps.explanation: 'Have any objection to me/my coming' is the formal equivalent of 'do you mind'.

gaps.lead: Reporters expect the trial to last several weeks.
gaps.explanation: 'Reporters expect it to last' becomes 'it is expected to last'.

gaps.lead: He is so impatient that he refuses to read instructions.
gaps.explanation: so impatient that he refuses = far too impatient to.
